timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: One security plan for all databases?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: No. SQL, NoSQL, and object storage each have their own attack surface.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Parameterized queries, least-privilege accounts, column and row-level security, encryption.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Database-per-tenant, schema-per-tenant, or shared table with row-level security.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Validate query operators — NoSQL injection is real. Per-application credentials, field encryption.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: The classic leak. Public access off by default, least-privilege bucket policies, encryption, logging.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Immutable retention. A backup you can't delete survives ransomware and mistakes.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: At rest and in transit, on every datastore, without exception.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So the storage plane is a crown jewel?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Treat the management plane like one. Least privilege there protects all the data below.
